summary: A listicle on wood-fired oven baking as a global culinary tradition, noting a resurgence in popularity as of September 1, 2023. It profiles chefs and bakers from Naples, Provence, Madrid, Austin, Beirut, Melbourne and Buenos Aires, each sharing a signature dish and how wood-fired heat and smoke shape it. The dishes range from Neapolitan pizza and French boule to tapas, brisket, manakish, lava cake and empanadas.
one_line: A global tour of wood-fired oven recipes, from Neapolitan pizza to Texas brisket, as shared by chefs and bakers in 2023.
key_facts: As of September 1, 2023, the note reports a notable resurgence in the popularity of wood-fired oven baking.
Gianni Romano, a pizza chef originally from Naples, shared his Neapolitan Margherita secrets on October 15, 2023, stressing high heat and quick cooking time.
Neapolitan pizza uses high-gluten flour, water, yeast and salt dough, with San Marzano tomato sauce, mozzarella di bufala and fresh basil.
Marie-Claire Fontaine, a boulangerie artisan in Provence, said a perfect boule depends on overnight fermentation of the dough; French ovens are fueled by oak or cherry wood.
Carlos García of Madrid explained Gambas al Ajillo, shrimp in garlicky oil cooked in a terracotta dish placed in the glowing embers of the wood fire.
Elijah Williams, a pitmaster in Austin, Texas, smokes brisket seasoned with salt, pepper and a hint of cayenne over oak and hickory for many hours.
Yasmin Haddad, a baker in Beirut, Lebanon, shared her family's manakish recipe, topped with za'atar (sumac, sesame seeds and thyme), cheese or ground meat.
Manakish is a popular street food often called the pizza of the Arab world.
Emma Richardson, a pastry chef from Melbourne, Australia, showcased a wood-fired chocolate lava cake on October 23, 2023, served hot with vanilla ice cream.
Lucas Martinez, a Buenos Aires chef, bakes Argentinian empanadas filled with spiced beef, olives and eggs, served with chimichurri sauce.
The note says the barbecue pit, though not a dome-shaped oven, embodies the same principle of control over heat and smoke as wood-fired cooking.
